newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on Morocco vegoil tender, snow.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on Morocco vegoil tender, snow.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on speculation that a Moroccan optional origin tender might have been for Canadian canola oil and concerns that several inches of snow will cut output, traders said.

"Somebody did this Moroccan tender -- maybe it was one of us. I heard a lot of farmers want to buy back their hedges because it'll be a while before they get back on the field and there's good prices out in the country," a trader said. U.S. export sources said Morocco bought 49,500 tonnes of optional origin soybean or canola oil for November/December delivery.
Japan bought 5,000 tonnes of canola, sources said.
November canola rose $3.40 to $437.20. "This is the worst futures crush margin since Nov started trading," a trader said. Volume was 5,975 lots or 119,500 tonnes with 500 hedges.
October flax rose $9.20 to $407.20. "There were only eight deliveries against the Oct -- the long is clearly in charge," a trader said.

November western barley rose $1.50 to $149.50 on feedlot buying, while February rose $1.70 to $153.80. Volume was 1,500. October feed wheat rose $0.60 to $198.50 on commercials in volume of 1,225. Cargill bought 40 December oats, up US$4.70 to US$126.20. UGG bought five December peas, down US$1 to US$206.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats)
